top_paper.title: SafeAgent: Runtime Guardrails for LLM-Based Agents via Formal Specification Monitoring
top_paper.abstract: As LLM-based agents are deployed in production environments, ensuring their safety at runtime becomes critical. We propose SafeAgent, a runtime monitoring framework that enforces formally specified guardrails on agent behavior. SafeAgent translates natural language safety policies into temporal logic specifications and monitors agent action sequences against these specs in real-time. When a violation is detected, SafeAgent can block, modify or request human confirmation for the offending action. We evaluate on AgentSafetyEval, a new benchmark with 500+ adversarial agent trajectories across web navigation, code execution and API interaction domains. SafeAgent blocks 94% of unsafe actions while maintaining 97% task completion on benign trajectories, significantly outperforming prompt-based safety approaches. The framework introduces only 3ms median overhead per action.

top_papers.title: AgentScope-PHP: A Multi-Agent Framework for Hierarchical Planning with Human-in-the-Loop
top_papers.abstract: We present AgentScope-PHP, a novel multi-agent framework that integrates hierarchical planning with human-in-the-loop feedback. Our approach decomposes complex tasks into a three-tier planning hierarchy: strategic planning, tactical decomposition, and operational execution. At each tier, a designated agent proposes plans and a human supervisor can intervene to redirect, reject or refine the plan. We evaluate on WebArena, SWE-bench and a new multi-turn dialogue planning benchmark PlanEval-200. Results show that AgentScope-PHP achieves 23% improvement in task completion rate over baseline multi-agent systems while reducing human intervention frequency by 40% after the first 3 turns. We open-source the full framework including the evaluation suite.

top_papers.title: ContextCircuit: Rewiring In-Context Learning through Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation
top_papers.abstract: We introduce ContextCircuit, a structured approach to retrieval-augmented generation that treats in-context examples as a circuit with explicit routing. Instead of flat retrieval, we organize retrieved passages into a directed acyclic graph where nodes represent knowledge chunks and edges represent logical dependencies. A lightweight graph neural network routes the LLM's attention across this structure during generation. Experiments on MUSR, HotpotQA and a new multi-hop reasoning benchmark CircuitBench show 18% improvement in multi-hop accuracy and 12% reduction in hallucination rate. Our ablation study demonstrates that the graph routing component is critical, accounting for 65% of the improvement.

top_papers.title: Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Efficient LLM Inference
top_papers.abstract: Speculative decoding has emerged as a promising technique to accelerate LLM inference without quality degradation. However, existing approaches use a fixed draft model regardless of the input distribution, leading to suboptimal acceptance rates. We propose AdaSpec, an adaptive draft model selection framework that dynamically routes inputs to different sized draft models based on predicted difficulty. A lightweight router trained with contrastive learning predicts which draft model maximizes the acceptance rate for each token sequence. On Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B backbones, AdaSpec achieves 2.8x-3.4x speedup (vs 1.9x-2.3x for fixed draft) with no quality degradation across MT-Bench, HumanEval and GSM8K. We release the router training code and evaluation pipeline.
top_papers.llm_reason: AdaSpec 针对Speculative Decoding的实际工程痛点——固定draft模型导致acceptance rate不稳定——提出了自适应路由方案。工程价值直接：(1) 在主流大模型(Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B)上实现2.8x-3.4x加速，远超固定draft方案；(2)开源router训练代码可立即集成到推理服务中；(3)推理加速直接转化为成本节约和用户体验提升。理论贡献相对适中（自适应路由思想并非全新），但工程落地度和证据强度非常高（多模型、多benchmark验证）。行动建议：优先在推理集群中试点评估。

top_papers.title: WorldModelBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating World Models in Interactive Environments
top_papers.abstract: World models are increasingly seen as critical infrastructure for embodied agents, game-playing systems and simulation-based planning. Yet no unified benchmark exists to compare world models across domains. We introduce WorldModelBench, covering 12 interactive environments from household navigation to Atari games to robotic manipulation. We evaluate 8 existing world models (Genie, UniSim, Diamond, Oasis, etc.) on prediction accuracy, temporal consistency, controllability and downstream task performance. Our findings reveal that no single world model excels across all dimensions: video-generation-based models lead visual fidelity but lag in action-conditioned controllability, while dynamics-model-based approaches show the opposite pattern. We propose a composite scoring rubric and open-source the full evaluation suite.

top_papers.title: Task-Adaptive Embedding Refinement via Test-time LLM Guidance
top_papers.abstract: We explore the effectiveness of an LLM-guided query refinement paradigm for extending the usability of embedding models to challenging zero-shot search and classification tasks. Our approach refines the embedding representation of a user query using feedback from a generative LLM on a small set of documents, enabling embeddings to adapt in real time to the target task. We conduct extensive experiments with state-of-the-art text embedding models across a diverse set of challenging search and clas
